chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Suleiman al-Ja'fary, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

The peacock is a morphed creature; it was a handsome man who insisted stubbornly upon the wife of a believing man who loved him, so he copulated with her. Then she sent messages to him afterwards, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, morphed both of them into peacocks, a female and a male. And their meat is not eaten, nor their eggs.
ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the peacock according to Shia hadith and why is its meat not eaten?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi links the physical transformation of a handsome man and a believing woman into peacocks to their specific sin of illicit intercourse, establishing the jurisprudential basis for the prohibition of consuming their meat and eggs. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of connecting zoological rulings to narrative origins, emphasizing that the impurity or distinctiveness of the animal stems from this divine morphing event.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The peacock was morphed, and it was a handsome man, so he insisted stubbornly a wife of a Believing man who loved him. So he copulated with her, then (she) sent messages to him (inviting him) afterwards. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Morphed both of them as peacocks, female and male, and neither eat their meats, nor their eggs’.
en.sarwar: 16. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Bakr ibn Salih from Sulayman al-Ja‘fariy who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The Peacock is metamorphosed. He was a beautiful man. He treated with disregard the woman of a believing man. The woman loved him and he fell on her, then continued and was metamorphosed by Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, in the form of male and female. It is not edible, in the form of flesh or its eggs.’”
